Shallow lagoon with mirror‑flat water and consistent thermal wind (300+ windy days per year); perfect for freestyle and learning; many kite schools and rental stations along the shore; accessible via Trapani–Birgi (Vincenzo Florio) Airport (TPS) 10 km away or Palermo Airport (PMO).

Wide sandy bay on Paros island with steady Meltemi winds (15–25 kn) in July, perfect for freeride and freestyle; flat inside near shore and small chop/waves further out. Several kite and windsurf schools along the beach, plus cafes and hotels. About 20 min drive from Paros National Airport (PAS) or ferry from Athens.

Thermally accelerated Meltemi winds (15–25+ knots) blow cross-shore in summer on this wide, shallow bay on the Gulf of Gökova. Flat water near shore with small chop further out; many kite schools and rental centres line the beach and town cafes/restaurants nearby. Fly into Dalaman Airport (DLM) and drive about 1.5 h to Akyaka.

Well‑maintained kitesurf beach inside El Gouna resort with steady side‑shore thermal winds (15–20 kn) in spring; flat waist‑deep water and high‑end facilities including gear storage, showers, bar and restaurant; close to El Gouna hotels; about a 30 min drive north of Hurghada International Airport (HRG).

Large turquoise bay on Egypt’s Red Sea near Safaga with steady north winds (18‑25 kn) in September. Huge shallow flat-water area for freestyle and foiling; several high-end hotels and kite centers offer rentals, lessons and rescue boats. Around 45 minutes south of Hurghada International Airport (HRG).

Part of Havana’s Playas del Este; wide sandy beach with steady side‑on NE trade winds in spring and small waves over sandy bottom; basic amenities and beach bars; kiters launch near the lifeguard tower; about a 30 min drive east of José Martí International Airport (HAV) in Havana.

Wide sandy bay in the Cabo de Gata‑Níjar Natural Park with side-on Levante winds in spring producing small waves; remote and undeveloped, so bring water and shade; access via car park and trail; about 1 h drive from Almería Airport (LEI) or 2.5 h from Málaga Airport (AGP).

Popular kitesurf spot on the Sea of Galilee with strong north winds (March–June) and warm, flat freshwater; the Kochav HaYam club offers a launching area and small cafe, with accommodations in nearby Tiberias; about a 2 h drive from Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) in Tel Aviv.

Sheltered bay on Sal Island with steady NE trade winds and flat, clear water; ideal for freestyle and foiling; numerous kite schools and beach bars; 5–10 min from Santa Maria and about 20 min from Amílcar Cabral International Airport (SID).

Trade-wind spot with strong winds and small to moderate waves. Kite area on Santa Maria's east side is ideal for experienced kiters; schools and rentals nearby. About a 20‑minute drive from Amílcar Cabral International Airport (SID).
Trade winds 15–25 kn Nov–Apr; moderate waves and water around 20–25 °C; beach has kite schools, rentals and bars.

Constant SE trade winds and a wide shallow lagoon protected by reef; world‑class waves (One Eye, Manawa) plus flat‑water sections; numerous kite schools and rental shops along the beach; reach via Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU) about 60 min drive.

This world‑famous spot has consistent 20‑30 kn SE trade winds in August, offering a mix of flat lagoon water and legendary reef breaks like One Eye and Manawa. Several kite centres and hotels line the beach at Le Morne, and it’s about a 1 h drive from Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU).

World-class waves and a huge flat lagoon with steady trade winds in January. Several kitesurf schools and gear rentals nearby. About a 60 min drive from Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU).

September brings strong SE trade winds at Le Morne due to a venturi effect. The large lagoon has flat sections and world‑class waves like One Eye and Manawa. Many kitesurf schools, rentals and resorts line the beach. About 1 hour’s drive from Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU).

Peninsula at southern tip of Rhodes where the Aegean and Mediterranean meet; meltemi winds funnel across a sandbar creating both flat-water and wave sides. Strong 20–30 kn cross/onshore winds in summer; kitesurf center on site; remote with few facilities; approx. 1.5 hr drive from Rhodes International Airport (RHO).

Long sandy beach on Naxos exposed to the Meltemi winds 15–25 kn in July. Parthena side offers flat water inside a rock reef; northern side has rolling waves for jumping. A few tavernas, small hotels and kite/windsurf centers nearby. About 20 min drive from Naxos Island National Airport (JNX) or ferry from Paros/Mykonos.

Remote bay near Diego Suarez with turquoise lagoon and strong cross‑shore winds (20–25 kn) throughout August; shallow flat water inside the reef and waves outside. A few kite camps and small hotels dot this unspoiled area. The nearest airport is Antsiranana (Diego Suarez) Airport (DIE) about 30 minutes away by road.

Remote bay in northern Madagascar near Diego Suarez with a turquoise lagoon and steady cross‑shore winds (around 20 kn) in July. Few kite camps and small hotels offer rentals and lessons; bring cash and supplies. About 30 min drive from Antsiranana (Diego Suarez) Airport (DIE).
Remote reef-protected lagoon; Varatraza trade wind mid-Mar–Nov (20–35 kn in May, Jun & Oct; 25–40 kn Jul–Sep); lodges on site; mix of flat water and waves.
Reef-protected lagoon in northern Madagascar; Varatraza trade wind mid-Mar–Nov with 20–35 kn in May, Jun & Oct, 25–40 kn Jul–Sep; remote spot with lodges and mix of flat water and waves.

Charming fishing village with consistent 20–30 kn trade winds in August; wide sandy beaches and dunes provide epic downwinders between Preá and Guriú. The town is lively with many pousadas, restaurants and kite centres. Nearest airport is Jericoacoara Regional Airport (JJD) about 30 min away or Fortaleza (FOR) 4 h by road.

Iconic fishing village turned kite mecca on Brazil’s Ceará coast; strong 20‑30 kn NE trade winds in November with downwinders to Preá and Tatajuba; long sandy beach and lagoons offer flat and small wave areas; lively town full of pousadas, restaurants, bars and kite centres; fly into Jericoacoara Regional Airport (JJD) 40 km away or Pinto Martins‑Fortaleza (FOR) about 4 hours’ drive.

Long sandy beach near Jericoacoara with strong, steady NE trade winds often exceeding 20 kn in August; wide launch area and choppy water ideal for big-air and downwinders. Several kite schools, pousadas and restaurants line the village. The nearest airport is Jericoacoara Regional Airport (JJD) about 30 min away or Fortaleza Airport (FOR) about 4 hours by road.
Long sandy beach near Jericoacoara; NE trades Jul–Feb with peak in Nov; accessible by buggy/4×4; several pousadas and beach restaurants.

Freshwater lagoon just inland from Cumbuco with mirror‑flat water and steady 18–25 kn NE trade winds in August; perfect for freestyle and beginners. Accessible by buggy or taxi from Cumbuco village; simple cafes and kite schools line the shore. Nearest airport is Pinto Martins–Fortaleza International Airport (FOR) about 45 minutes away.

Freshwater lagoon just behind the dunes at Cumbuco with butter‑flat water and steady 18‑25 kn NE trade winds in late spring; ideal for freestyle and beginners; reached by buggy or taxi from Cumbuco village; simple beach shacks sell drinks and snacks—no facilities; nearest airport is Pinto Martins–Fortaleza (FOR) around 40 km away.

Long sandy beach on the Giens Peninsula with steady Mistral and thermal winds of around 15–25 kn in August; shallow water and open bay make it ideal for freeride and foiling. There are kite schools, rental shops and parking along the beach. The nearest airport is Toulon–Hyères Airport (TLN) about 10 min away, or Marseille Airport (MRS) 1.5 h by car.

Turquoise shallow lagoon on Rodrigues Island with steady 18‑25 kn trade winds in August; wide sandy beach and reef-protected lagoon ideal for all levels; small kite schools and hotels around Mourouk; nearest airport is Sir Gaëtan Duval Airport (RRG) about 45 min away via flights from Mauritius.

August winds blow regularly at 15‑20 knots from the east in this bay, offering flat water inside the reef and small waves outside. Cabarete village has many kite schools, gear rental shops, bars and accommodation. The nearest airport is Gregorio Luperón International Airport (POP) about 30 minutes away.

Famous kitesurf beach with steady 15‑20 knot trade winds and thermals in June; flat water inside the reef and small waves outside; lively Cabarete village offers many kite schools, rentals, bars and restaurants; about a 30‑minute drive from Gregorio Luperón International Airport (POP) near Puerto Plata.

Famous kitesurfing beach with consistent trade winds in May; flat water inside the reef and small waves outside; lively village offers numerous kite schools, rental shops, bars and restaurants; about a 30 min drive from Gregorio Luperón International Airport (POP) near Puerto Plata.

Little-developed island in the Sulu Sea with buttery-flat lagoons and constant NE trade winds in Dec‑Jan. Ride over turquoise, waist-deep water with sandy bottom; village of Cuyo offers basic guesthouses and eateries. Travel by small plane to Cuyo Airport or ferry/flight via Puerto Princesa or Manila.

Remote resort on Pagudpud's north coast with powerful NE trade winds and rolling waves over reef. Kite from the beach out front; resort provides rooms, restaurant, gear rental and rescue boat. Best for intermediate riders. Reachable via Laoag (LAO) or Tuguegarao (TUG) airports, 1–2 h by road.

Wide sand spit where the Breede River meets the ocean. Consistent SE winds blow December‑March; flat water in the river mouth and choppy wave in the surf zone. Remote village with a few guesthouses and restaurants—bring supplies. About 3 h drive from Cape Town or 2 h from George (GRJ) airport.

Long stretch of beach north of Cape Town with strong SE "Cape Doctor" winds (20–30 kn) in summer; the main kite launch is at Dolphin Beach/Kite Beach near Table View. Expect small waves and chop. Numerous kite schools, rentals, bars and restaurants line the beachfront. About 20 min from Cape Town Intl Airport (CPT).

Small uninhabited island off Union Island accessible by boat; flat turquoise lagoon with steady 15–25 kn trade winds and waist-deep water, perfect for freestyle; kite schools operate from anchored boats; bring drinking water & sun protection; nearest airport is Union Island (UNI) or flights via Barbados.

Shallow knee-deep lagoon protected by reef with steady NE trade winds (~15–20 kn). Perfect for beginners and freestyle. Small grassy rigging area with beach bars and restrooms nearby. Located in Le Vauclin on Martinique’s Atlantic side about 30 min from Aime Cesaire Intl Airport (FDF).

Cross-onshore SE winds with shallow, flat lagoon perfect for learners; launch from Shark Bay sandbar and watch tide & shells. 95% wind reliability in summer. Nearby Langebaan offers kite schools, restaurants and accommodation. About 1 h north of Cape Town Intl Airport (CPT).

Shallow, flat‑water lagoon near Langebaan with 95% wind reliability in summer. Ideal for beginners and freeriders; cafes and rental shops nearby. About 130 km north of Cape Town International Airport (CPT).

Flat-water lagoon ideal for beginners; high wind reliability in January (around 95%) with shallow warm water. About 130 km north of Cape Town International Airport (CPT), with good facilities in Langebaan.

Broad white‑sand beach with shallow turquoise lagoon and reliable cross‑shore winds (Kusi in Jun–Oct, Kaskazi in Dec–Mar). Several kite centres and a relaxed village atmosphere. Around 60 km from Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ) in Zanzibar City.

Wide tidal lagoon on Zanzibar’s east coast with steady cross-shore trade winds (15–20 kn) in July. Shallow turquoise water ideal for beginners, many kite schools, gear hire and beach bars. About 1 h drive from Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ) in Zanzibar City.

Wide beach and tidal lagoon on Zanzibar’s east coast with 15–20 knot cross‑shore trade winds in June; shallow turquoise water inside the reef and small waves outside; numerous kite schools, gear rentals, beach bars and restaurants line the village; about a 1‑hour drive from Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ) in Zanzibar City.

Large flat-water lagoon with year-round winds (~70–80% reliability in winter). On-site camp offers accommodations and kitesurf facilities. Access via Dakhla Airport (VIL) with flights via Casablanca or Agadir.

Located on Dakhla’s vast shallow lagoon with 25–30 kn trade winds in July. Flat water perfect for freestyle and a launch point for wave trips to Speed Spot and Lassarga. On-site camp offers accommodation, restaurant, gear rental and rescue boat. Access via Dakhla Airport (VIL) with connections via Casablanca or Agadir.

Camp located on Dakhla’s huge shallow lagoon with steady 20‑25 knot winds in June; offers flat water for freestyle and easy access to nearby wave spots; on-site camp provides accommodation, restaurant, gear rental and rescue boat; accessible via Dakhla Airport (VIL) with connections through Casablanca or Agadir.

Popular beach town on the Riviera Maya with warm Caribbean waters and moderate trade winds in winter. Good base for excursions to Isla Blanca lagoon and Cozumel; numerous kite schools and amenities. Approximately a 45‑min drive south of Cancún International Airport (CUN).

Long sandy beach at Tarifa’s edge with reliable Levante and Poniente winds. Numerous kite schools, rental shops and lively beach bars. Approximately a 1.5 h drive from Málaga‑Costa del Sol Airport (AGP) or 45 min from Gibraltar Airport (GIB).

Long sandy beach in Tarifa with Levante and Poniente winds creating both flat water and choppy conditions; vibrant kite scene with many schools, rental shops and beach bars; head north for more space; about 1.5 h drive from Málaga Airport (AGP) or 45 min from Gibraltar Airport (GIB).

Long sandy beach in Tarifa with constant Levante and Poniente winds in September. Inside the bay there are flat areas and small chops; Europe's kite mecca with numerous schools, rentals and beach bars. About 1.5 h drive from Malaga (AGP) or 45 min from Gibraltar (GIB) airports.
Popular kitesurf spot on Fehmarn’s south coast with shallow waters and steady winds in spring. Nearby camping sites and surf schools. Approximately a 2.5 h drive from Hamburg Airport (HAM).

Wide sandy beach near Burj Al Arab with moderate temperatures in February and steady onshore winds. Facilities include showers, cafes and rentals. About 30 min drive from Dubai International Airport (DXB).

Primary kitesurf beach on Boracay’s east side with steady Amihan trade winds (Nov–Mar) and a shallow lagoon. Busy scene with many kite schools, bars and restaurants. Reachable via Caticlan Airport (MPH) or Kalibo International Airport (KLO) plus boat transfer.

Large shallow lagoon with reliable winds around 15‑25 kn during December – March. Great for beginners and freestylers; several kite camps and guesthouses on the sand spit. About a 3‑hour drive from Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) near Colombo.

Large shallow lagoon with strong SW monsoon winds (20‑30 kn) in July. Many kite camps offer lessons, gear rental and rescue boats; village vibe with limited nightlife. About 3 h by road from Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) near Colombo.

Large shallow lagoon with steady 20‑30 knot SW monsoon winds in June; numerous kite camps line the shores offering lessons, gear rental and downwinders; remote fishing-village vibe with limited amenities; roughly a 3‑hour drive north of Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) near Colombo.

Wide sandy bay in Rockingham with shallow sandbar and consistent 15‑25 kn seabreezes from November to March; flat waist‑deep water ideal for beginners and freestyle; grassy rigging area, toilets and showers, parking and nearby kite schools; 45 min drive south of Perth and about 50 min from Perth Airport (PER).

Secluded islet within Nonsuch Bay with flat, crystal‑clear water and steady northeast trade winds. Popular for boat‑based sessions; arrange trips with local schools as there are no facilities on the island. Launch from Nonsuch Bay on the mainland about 30 km by road from V. C. Bird International Airport (ANU) in St. John’s.

Charming fishing village on Brazil’s northeast coast with consistent trade winds and flat‑water lagoons plus small wave spots like Ponta de Santo Cristo. Several kite schools and pousadas in town. Around 110 km from São Gonçalo do Amarante – Governador Aluizio Alves International Airport (NAT) in Natal.

Warm tropical bay with consistent trade winds and a mix of flat‑water lagoon and reef waves. Vibrant kitesurf scene with gear rentals and schools in town. Approximately 20 km from Gregorio Luperón International Airport (POP) at Puerto Plata.

World-class wind spot on Gran Canaria's east coast with strong NE trade winds (20–35 knots) and choppy waves that attract windsurfing competitions. Pebbly beach and rocky reef; launch can be tricky but there are several wind/kite schools, gear shops and cafes in town. Best from July–August; fly into Las Palmas/Gran Canaria Airport (LPA) about 20 min away.

Long sandy beach south of Sotavento offering cross-shore NE trades in summer; back-up spot when Sotavento lagoon is too full; moderate chop with some waves; a few rental centers and hotels nearby; roughly 1 h drive south of Fuerteventura Airport (FUE).

Wide tidal lagoon on Fuerteventura's Sotavento beach with consistent NE trade winds (15–30 kn) in summer. Ideal for speed runs and freeride with flat, shallow water at low tide; wave conditions outside lagoon. Home of René Egli kite center with rentals and lessons. About 60 min drive south from Fuerteventura Airport (FUE).

Quiet wave spot 20 km south of Essaouira with stronger side-shore trade winds in July and rolling Atlantic waves. Wide sandy beach with a few surf lodges and cafes; less crowded than Essaouira. About 30 min drive from Essaouira town and Mogador Airport (ESU) or 3 h from Marrakech (RAK).

Wide sandy beach 20 km south of Essaouira with consistent trade winds and Atlantic swells in September – perfect for wave riding. A few surf lodges and cafes provide rentals and meals. Reachable via Essaouira‑Mogador Airport (ESU) or about 3 hours drive from Marrakech (RAK).

4 km-long bay with 20–25 kn trade winds in July thanks to the venturi effect. Safe shallow water with sections of chop and small waves; numerous kite schools, rentals and cafes along the promenade. Reachable via Essaouira‑Mogador Airport (ESU) or about 2 h drive from Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK).

4 km‑long bay with steady 20‑30 knot trade winds in June caused by thermal and venturi effects; wide sandy beach with shallow water for safe launch and waves building toward the downwind end; numerous kite schools, gear rentals and cafes along the promenade; reachable via Essaouira‑Mogador Airport (ESU) or a 2‑hour drive from Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK).

10 km-long beach with steady trade winds (10‑20 knots) and a safe bay; lots of kite schools and equipment rentals; lively medina nearby; reach via Essaouira‑Mogador Airport (ESU) or 2‑3 hr drive from Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK).

10 km‑long sandy bay facing the Atlantic with steady trade winds (15–25 kn) through autumn; flat water near the harbour and small waves downwind; dozens of kite schools and rental shops along the promenade; historic medina and restaurants steps away; fly into Essaouira‑Mogador Airport (ESU) or drive 2 – 3 hours from Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK).
Warm shallow waters and NE/E cross-onshore winds averaging 18 kn (22 kn in summer); winds strongest in afternoons; beach park has grassy rigging area and showers.
Sheltered bay with butter-flat water upwind and waves downwind; best wind mid-Jun–mid-Sep (16–24 kn); remote area with only two restaurants nearby; car recommended.
Sheltered bay with butter-flat water upwind and waves downwind; best wind mid-June to mid-September (16–24 kn) but season runs May–October; remote area with only two restaurants; car recommended.
Mountain lake where Maloja thermal winds blow Jun–Aug (10–18 kn); launch from grassy meadow; water is cold (5/4 mm wetsuit needed); local club offers restaurant, showers, camping & parking.
Side-shore freeride spot; wind season Apr–Oct (15–30 kn Jul–Sep); caution with volcanic rocks at low tide.
Barrier island with steady winds; spring sees a mix of SW and NE winds; wide beaches with shallow sound-side waters; car rental essential; plenty of surf shops and rental houses.
High-wind heaven from October to March; fierce winds blow across these islands; rent a scooter or car as public transport is limited; best for experienced riders.

Constant trade winds (20+ knots) and warm shallow waters make El Yaque a freestyle paradise; many kite schools, hotels and restaurants line the beachfront; lively but relaxed atmosphere; access via Santiago Mariño Caribbean International Airport (PMV) on Margarita Island or via Caracas (CCS).

Stretch of beach near Santa Verónica with steady 20‑25 knot trades and waves over the outer reef; authentic local vibe with a few kite camps and small hotels; limited facilities—bring your own gear; about 45 min drive from Barranquilla’s Ernesto Cortissoz International Airport (BAQ) or 2 hr from Cartagena’s Rafael Núñez Airport (CTG).

Wide sandy beach on Boa Vista's west coast with consistent NE trade winds in May and small chop/waves; remote area with a few beach bars and kite schools; accessible via Aristides Pereira International Airport (BVC) about a 10‑minute drive from Sal Rei.

Remote beach north of Malindi with golden sand and reliable side‑shore thermal winds in May (~15‑25 kn); the kitesurf centre offers lessons and rentals alongside a rustic eco-lodge; amenities are basic so bring cash and supplies; about a 45 min drive from Malindi Airport (MYD) or 2 h from Moi International Airport (MBA) in Mombasa.

Beach and lagoon near Fortaleza with steady side-on NE trade winds (15–25 kn) starting in May; wide sandy beach backed by dunes, with numerous kite schools, rental centers and pousadas; about a 45 min drive west of Pinto Martins–Fortaleza International Airport (FOR).

Remote bay at the edge of Western Australia’s Ningaloo Reef famous for long peeling waves and 15‑25 kn trade winds in spring; reef passes deliver world‑class wave sailing and flat water inside sections; stay at Gnaraloo Station campground with basic facilities—bring supplies and a 4WD; nearest airports are Carnarvon Airport (CVQ) or Learmonth (LEA) about 3 – 5 hours’ drive.

Long powder‑white beach on Miyakojima with warm turquoise water and consistent 15‑20 kn north‑easterly trades in November; wide shallow area perfect for beginners and reef break for wave riders; amenities include cafes, gear rental and showers; fly to Miyako Airport (MMY) or Shimojishima Airport (SHI) via connections from Naha.

Small remote island in Okinawa offering uncrowded kiting on long sandy beaches such as Eef Beach; reliable 15‑20 kn north‑easterly trades in November with flat water and small waves over reef; limited hotels and restaurants in Kume town—book in advance; fly via Naha Airport (OKA) and connect to Kumejima Airport (UEO) about 2 km from the beaches.
High‑wind heaven Oct–Mar; archipelago with fierce winds; rent a scooter/car due to limited public transport; better for experienced riders.
Cape Doctor cross-onshore winds Oct–Mar; wave spot near Table View; many restaurants, surf shops and rentals along the beachfront.
Emerald Sea lagoon fed by strong Varatraza wind mid‑Mar–Nov; remote eco‑lodge with reef‑protected flat water and waves.
Shallow lagoon ideal for kitesurfing with consistent moderate winds Apr–Oct; flat water and nearby kite schools, rentals, restaurants and picnic areas.
Shallow lagoon ideal for kitesurfing with consistent moderate winds Apr–Oct; flat water and nearby kite schools, rentals, restaurants and picnic areas.

Vast protected lagoon in Namibia’s Walvis Bay with consistent 25‑35 kn thermal winds in spring and autumn; flat shallow water and long reaches ideal for speed runs; cold water with strong currents and seals—wear a wetsuit; limited facilities but town offers hotels and restaurants; fly into Walvis Bay International Airport (WVB) 15 km away or drive 30 min from Swakopmund.

Large bay on Peru's south coast with reliable cross‑shore winds (15–25 kn) from September to May; flat water inside the bay and small chop outside; several kite schools and hotels in Paracas town; easiest access via Capitán FAP Renán Elías Olivera Airport (PIO) in Pisco or 3‑hour drive from Lima’s Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM).

Famous left-hand wave in northern Peru with long, peeling rides powered by SW trade winds in October. The bay offers flat water near the point and rolling waves downwind. Small fishing town with a few hostels and kite/surf schools. Fly into Chiclayo (CIX) or Trujillo (TRU) and drive 2 hours north to Pacasmayo.

Legendary flat‑water strip along Dakhla lagoon. A sandbar creates mirror‑smooth water at mid‑ to low tide with strong, consistent winds – perfect for speed runs and freestyle. There are no facilities; excursions depart from kite camps. Access via boat or 4×4 from camps; nearest airport is Dakhla (VIL).

Spectacular spot on Dakhla lagoon where a white sand dune forms a natural ramp. Constant cross‑offshore winds provide flat water at low tide and small waves at high tide. Very remote – trips are organised from kite camps. Access via 4×4 or boat from Dakhla; nearest airport is Dakhla (VIL).
